title: platform-standup-2026-03-11
content:
Attendees: Ava, Marcus, Priya, Liam, Zoe (brief check-ins from SRE on pager coverage)

Summary / High-level: quick standup focused on control plane rollout, routing policy migration, quota enforcement changes, and an auth regression affecting scheduled jobs. Most items are follow-ups or small fixes; one larger change (routing policy rollout) is on track for canary tomorrow.

Yesterday / Progress highlights:
- Control plane: completed smoke tests for the new routing policy engine (policy-v2). Deterministic routing tests passed on staging (1000 requests/day sim). Marcus finished the policy TTL improvements to reduce stale assignments.
- Routing: implemented route fallback mapping for model variants; initial metrics show 8% lower tail latency on canary nodes.
- Auth: rolled an emergency patch to refresh service-account token caching after we saw ~120 401s for scheduled-batch jobs on Friday. Patch (PR #989) deployed to staging; appears to stabilize token refresh logic.
- Quotas: added temporary throttle rule for unbounded embedding ingestion from internal QA team; prevented a repeat of yesterday's quota spike (peak 2.4x normal). Priya instrumented more detailed quota-exhaustion logs.

Blockers / Risks:
- Control plane canary depends on a missing migration script (db index) that could increase deployment time if not applied in the maintenance window. Action: Liam to open DB migration PR and coordinate with release-engineering (OWNER: Liam; ETA: EOD 2026-03-11).
- Auth regression root cause still not fully identified: patch mitigates symptoms but doesn't explain intermittent token expiry for long-running jobs. Need deeper trace. Action: Zoe and Marcus to add distributed trace spans for token lifecycle and reproduce with long-running job harness (ACTION by 2026-03-12).
- Quotas: our emergency throttle prevented customer impact but customer-visible quota signals are noisy. We need to standardize quota error responses. Action: Priya to draft spec for quota error payloads and retry guidance (draft by 2026-03-13).

Today / Next steps:
- Control plane: canary rollout of policy-v2 to 10% of traffic tomorrow morning. Tasks: finalize migration script, update rollout docs, schedule canary watchdog. (Owner: Marcus / Liam)
- Routing: monitor tail latency and reroute behavior for model-fallback; add dashboard panels for per-model fallback rate (Owner: Marcus).
- Auth: add more detailed logging and a synthetic long-running job test to reproduce token expiry. (Owner: Zoe + Marcus)
- Quotas: update quota-exhaustion logging schema and add example client retry behavior to the docs. (Owner: Priya)

Decisions made:
- Proceed with policy-v2 canary tomorrow at 08:00 PT with 10% traffic. Manual rollback threshold: >2% increase in p95 latency or any 5xx error rate increase.
- Emergency throttle rules will remain in place until quota error payloads are standardized and clients are updated (expected ~1 week).

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Liam: open DB migration PR for control-plane (ETA EOD 2026-03-11).
- Marcus: finalize rollout playbook and add canary watchdog cron (ETA 2026-03-11 morning).
- Zoe & Marcus: instrument token lifecycle traces; reproduce with long-job harness (ETA 2026-03-12).
- Priya: draft quota error payload spec + example client retry guidance (ETA 2026-03-13).
- Ava: update oncall runbook with new auth troubleshooting steps and add link to PR #989 (ETA 2026-03-11).

Notes / context / links:
- Staging run results: small perf gain on tail latency after routing changes, but increased CPU on canary nodes under synthetic load (see staging-metrics snapshot). Need to validate under real traffic shape.
- Related tickets: JIRA-PLAT-4123 (routing policy engine), JIRA-PLAT-4150 (auth token expiry investigation), JIRA-PLAT-4162 (quota error standardization).
- Slack channels: #eng-platform, #oncall, #platform-rollouts.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we automatically evict stale routing assignments when node heartbeats are missed for >30s? (Tentative: yes, but throttle eviction rate to avoid flapping.)
- Do customers need an explicit header/field indicating quota source (user vs. team vs. system)? If yes, we should add to the quota payload schema.

Quick personal notes (informal):
- Keep an eye on canary CPU — if we see >15% host CPU increase we may need to reduce max-batch-size on canary only.
- Follow up with Zendesk case #2346 about a customer seeing unexpected quota errors last week (linked to the noisy quota signal).

Next standup: 2026-03-12 09:30 PT (same channel).

---
Raw snippets / scratch notes:
- "policy-v2": needs TTL tweak + DB index to look up routing keys faster.
- Temporary throttle config path: /configs/quotas/temporary-throttle/qa-ingest
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/989 (auth patch), https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/992 (routing-fallback)
